skipReasons.electron/knowledge/knowledge-store.ts: depends on the Boss commander durable-json layer, which would drag a runtime into this module

layout.contracts/: value shapes, required/optional field lists and the query field list
layout.retrieval/: entry matching, budgeted retrieval, goal reranking and planRetrieval
layout.taxonomy/: taxonomy derivation and the deterministic domain router
layout.trust/: trust order, trust floor and the trust-then-recency ordering

adaptation: TypeScript -> ESM JavaScript; the algorithms are unchanged (trust ordering, all-tag matching, validity windows, character budget, tokeniser weights).
conflictReport() and planRetrieval() were added on top of the donor surface so supersession/conflict metadata and goal-driven assembly each have one home.
entryMatches() accepts an explicit `now` for deterministic tests instead of always reading Date.now().
The donor's knowledge-store.ts was not copied at all, so this module has no storage, no durable-json dependency and no Boss runtime requirement.
The module is split into contracts/retrieval/taxonomy/trust/conflict facades over a single core implementation, so consumers can import a narrow surface without duplicating algorithms.
knownDifferences: No persistence: the module is pure, and the incubator room holds catalogs in the page only.
No embeddings, no vector store, no LLM summarisation.
No domain route/rerank outside the deterministic tokeniser (the donor has no embeddings either).

vectors: trust ordering HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW > UNVERIFIED and unknown trust = 0
domain filter, shelf filter, all-tag matching
character budget truncation and larger-budget behaviour
taxonomy derivation (domains, shelves, tags sorted and de-duplicated)
deterministic domain router (domain match then up to three shared tags, no match routes nowhere)
relevance weights (title 3x, tags 2x, domain 2x, content 1x) and rerank order
supersession/conflict metadata including dangling supersedes pointers
